comments.body:
Root-cause evidence (session a85e3cd3, worktree fix-nabarlek at origin/main a8cf8fffc2a, 2026-11-03 23:3x PST):

Observation:
- Deterministic repro on current main: `pytest -n 2 -o timeout=20 tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` -> `[gw0] node down: Not properly terminated`, `rebar crash guard: xdist worker=gw0 terminated abnormally: Not properly terminated`, `worker 'gw0' crashed while running ...test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir`, FAILED with no traceback and no pytest-timeout banner in the controller output. Byte-for-byte the shape in all 3 saved make-verify logs (fix-caudata gw1, fix-manta gw3, fix-chihuahua gw3).
- Mechanism: pyproject sets timeout=300, timeout_method="thread"; thread-method expiry calls os._exit(1) in the worker (documented in pyproject and test_timeout_budget_headroom.py), and the stack dump never reaches the controller log.
- The test is one item that re-runs 14 real tests (test_opcert_service.py + test_opcert_service_integrity.py) serially under ONE 300 s budget. Cost on current main, run alone: 82.07 s call at load 35; nested modules 83.41 s at load 28 (about 18 s CPU, the rest waiting). Gerrit 3283 recorded 236 s for the 2 modules at load 40 (was 412 s), i.e. 1.27x headroom under 300 s.
- The 3 crashed runs took 3 h 45 min to 4 h 51 min (normal 20-25 min, about 10x slowdown), and none contained 5908e0d311d (Gerrit 3283).
- OOM excluded for 2026-11-03: macOS unified log (jetsam predicate, read-only) records 2 jetsam kills that day, both Apple daemons (per-process-limit), no python process.
- Nested pytest's own timeout excluded: run_nested_pytest passes timeout=None here, and a nested per-test timeout would fail the assert with output, not kill the worker.

Conclusion: the worker is killed by pytest-timeout's thread method when the aggregated nested run exceeds the 300 s per-test budget under heavy host slowdown. 3283 widened the margin but did not remove the mechanism; with about 10x slowdown the current 236 s-at-load-40 cost can still exceed 300 s.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
During slow, heavily loaded `make verify` runs (3 h 45 min to 4 h 51 min, against the usual 20 to 25 min), xdist workers died in `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py::test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir`. The crash guard printed `terminated abnormally: Not properly terminated`, and pytest printed no traceback. This happened 3 times on 2026-11-03 PST (fix-caudata gw1, fix-manta gw3, fix-chihuahua gw3). The test passes when run alone.

## Root cause (evidence in the comment of 2026-11-03 23:4x PST)
- `pyproject.toml` `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` sets `timeout = 300` and `timeout_method = "thread"`. When the budget runs out, the thread method calls `os._exit(1)` inside the worker (see the comment block above `timeout = 300` in `pyproject.toml`, and `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py`). So the timeout shows up as a node-down with no traceback.
- The test is a single item that runs `tests/_nested_pytest.py::run_nested_pytest` (`timeout=None`) over the 14 tests in `tests/unit/test_opcert_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_opcert_service_integrity.py`, one after another, all under one 300 s budget.
- Measured cost on main `a8cf8fffc2a`: 82.07 s call alone at load average 35. Gerrit 3283 (`5908e0d311d`, which none of the 3 crashed runs contained) measured 236 s at load 40. That leaves only 1.27x headroom.
- Deterministic repro on current main: `pytest -n 2 -o timeout=20 tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` reproduces the exact node-down, no-traceback shape.
- A memory kill is ruled out: the macOS jetsam log for 2026-11-03 records no kill of any python process.

## Approach
Follow the escape that `pyproject.toml` already documents for a test that legitimately runs long: a plain `@pytest.mark.timeout(N)` with a one-line comment saying why.
- Give the tortoise test `@pytest.mark.timeout(900)`, with a comment citing the measured costs: 82 s alone and 236 s at load 40.
- 900 s covers the 82 s measurement times the roughly 10x slowdown seen in the crashed runs. It is also 3.8x the 236 s figure, more than the 2.0x `_REQUIRED_HEADROOM` in `test_timeout_budget_headroom.py`.
- It stays below the 1 h CI job cap, so the test is still guarded against hangs.
- The test keeps the nested runtime check. That is its purpose: catching a key-copy leak that only appears when the signer modules actually run.

Out of scope: making thread-method timeout kills report as timeouts instead of silent crashes. That is filed as `delighted-worthless-foal` (discovered_from this ticket).

## Scope
- `tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py`: add the marker and its comment.
- `tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py`: add a regression test, using the existing `_timeout_marker_seconds` helper, that pins the tortoise test's marker at 900 s or more.

## Testing
- New test first (red): `test_tortoise_nested_signer_run_marker_covers_loaded_cost` in `test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` asserts the marker on `test_signer_test_modules_leave_no_key_copy_in_the_temp_dir` is not None and is at least 900 s. It fails before the marker is added because `_timeout_marker_seconds` returns None.
- Behavior check before and after: `pytest -n 2 -o timeout=20 tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py`. Before the fix it reports `1 failed, 5 passed` with a node-down. After the fix, the marker overrides the shrunken ini budget, so the result is `6 passed` with no node-down.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0, run with the worktree `.venv/bin` first on PATH.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The cause of the gw1 death is identified with recorded evidence (exit signal or log line) in a comment on this ticket.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/test_timeout_budget_headroom.py` passes, including the new `test_tortoise_nested_signer_run_marker_covers_loaded_cost`, which failed before the marker was added.
- [ ] `pytest -n 2 -o timeout=20 tests/unit/test_opcert_key_copy_leak_tortoise.py` reports 6 passed and no `node down`.
- [ ] `make lint` and `make typecheck` exit 0 in the worktree.
- [ ] The fix's Gerrit change is merged with LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
